payload.reason: The evidence provides specific details about previously reported results in speculation detection and scope resolution using various models, including improvements in F1 scores over prior benchmarks.

claims.text: Substantial improvements were reported over previously reported results by at least 0.29 F1 points on cue detection and 4.27 F1 points on scope resolution.
XLNet consistently outperformed BERT and RoBERTa in negation detection and scope resolution, contrary to results on other benchmark datasets.
State-of-the-art results were achieved on negation scope resolution for the BioScope Corpus and SFU Review Corpus, with specific F1 point increases reported.
